answer: Behavioural kinship scoring links seats secretly run by one operator. Each epoch every seat answers a shared audit task, such as predicting tide heights for a harbor or estimating the ferrous content of an ore sample, while the network logs response latency and token rhythm and computes pairwise correlation. Seats above 0.8 merge into one kin group sharing a single reward slot, so 100 clones on one GPU collapse into one payout, 1% each. Random delays don't mask the shared token rhythm; passing as independent needs 100 separate machines, a cost paid per seat that can't be pooled.
